meta.title: Speak English with confidence — Empire English Community
meta.description: A training system for Arabic speakers: daily practice on the platform, a live session every week, and a level measured precisely against a recognised scale.

hero.title: You understand English. But when it is your turn to speak, nothing comes out.
hero.subtitle: The problem is not that you do not know enough. It is that you have never practised getting it out loud, every day, with someone correcting you.
hero.ctaPrimary: Start with the level test — free
hero.reassure: The test is free and commits you to nothing. It measures your level against a recognised scale and tells you where to begin.

problem.eyebrow: Why nothing has worked so far
problem.title: Not intelligence. Method.

points.title: Years of study, almost no speaking
points.body: Grammar, vocabulary, endless lectures — all of it input. The skill you actually want is output, and that is precisely what nobody ever made you do.

points.title: Apps do not make you speak
points.body: You tap the right word and earn a point. Fine. But a real conversation has a person in front of you waiting for your answer, and no app has ever trained you for that.

points.title: A new tutor every month
points.body: Without one consistent system and real follow-up, you restart from zero each time. Consistency beats intensity — and consistency needs structure.

system.title: Three layers. Only one of them has a schedule.
system.intro: Most people assume the live session is the training. Here it is not. The training happens every day on your own, and the session is for correction and accountability.

layers.title: Practice with no appointment
layers.body: A practice platform open around the clock. Record yourself, drill pronunciation, review, repeat as often as you like — at three in the morning if that is when you are free.

layers.title: A community that notices you
layers.body: A space for students holding your daily tasks, your recordings and your streak. Your presence is visible, and that is what keeps you going.

layers.title: A live session for correction
layers.body: An hour with me every week. Not a lecture — a review of your specific mistakes, pronunciation correction, and next week's plan.

honest.title: One thing said plainly
honest.body: The weekly session is a group. You will not spend an hour speaking alone, and anyone promising you that inside a group is not being straight with you. The value of that hour is that an expert hears you, corrects you and holds you to account. The real repetition happens in the two layers above, and those are open to you all day.

placement.title: Find out your real level first
placement.body: An adaptive test across four skills that returns a specific level, not a rough guess. Free, no commitment, and its result is the basis of any plan that follows.
placement.note: After the test, if you want to continue, we book a live assessment — and its fee is credited in full against your first month.

faq.title: The questions that come up most

items.q: I am close to a complete beginner. Will this work?
items.a: Yes, and that describes most people who start with us. The path begins at the first level, and the explanation is in Arabic at the start, reducing gradually.

items.q: I live outside Egypt. Will the times suit me?
items.a: Sessions run on Cairo time, and the Gulf is only an hour or two ahead — so the same times work without anyone staying up late.

items.q: Will I sound like a native speaker?
items.a: No, and anyone promising you that does not believe it either. The goal is a clear, understandable American accent spoken with confidence. That is realistic and it can be measured.

items.q: What if I miss a session?
items.a: The daily practice is open and tied to no appointment, so missing a session does not stop your progress. We pick up what you missed in the next one.

items.q: How much time does it need each day?
items.a: Twenty to thirty minutes a day is enough if you are consistent. Consistency matters more than long, occasional bursts.

items.q: Why is the price in Egyptian pounds different?
items.a: Deliberately. Prices in pounds are set for income levels in Egypt, and international prices are for residents abroad. The system itself is identical either way.
From Egypt: mobile wallet or bank transfer. From abroad: international transfer or an online wallet. The details appear once you have chosen a plan.

items.q: What if I want to stop?
items.a: Membership is monthly and stops when you ask. Your data and progress are kept, so if you come back later you continue from the same point.
